verses.text: For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentiles...
Surely you have heard about the stewardship of God's grace that was given to me for you,
that is, the mystery made known to me by revelation, as I have already written briefly.
In reading this, then, you will be able to understand my insight into the mystery of Christ,
which was not made known to men in other generations as it has now been revealed by the Spirit to God's holy apostles and prophets.
This mystery is that through the gospel the Gentiles are fellow heirs, fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus.
I became a servant of this gospel by the gift of God's grace, given me through the working of His power.
Though I am less than the least of all the saints, this grace was given me: to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
and to illuminate for everyone the stewardship of this mystery, which for ages past was kept hidden in God, who created all things.
His purpose was that now, through the church, the manifold wisdom of God should be made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms,
according to the eternal purpose that He accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.
In Him and through faith in Him we may enter God's presence with boldness and confidence.
So I ask you not to be discouraged because of my sufferings for you, which are your glory.
... for this reason I bow my knees before the Father,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth derives its name.
I ask that out of the riches of His glory He may strengthen you with power through His Spirit in your inner being,
so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith. Then you, being rooted and grounded in love,
will have power, together with all the saints, to comprehend the length and width and height and depth
of the love of Christ, and to know this love that surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to Him who is able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine, according to His power that is at work within us,
to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen.

context.author: Paul the apostle (1:1; 3:1), though some scholars question this
context.genre: Letter, part prayer and part teaching, with a very long opening sentence
context.audience: Believers in Ephesus and probably nearby churches (the oldest manuscripts lack “in Ephesus” in 1:1)
context.setting: Paul calls himself a prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of the Gentiles, writing probably from Rome. He explains the mystery revealed to him: Gentiles are fellow heirs and members of one body. Then he bows his knees and prays that his readers will be strengthened, rooted in love, and know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge.
context.custom: “Mystery” in Greek religions meant secrets known only to initiates. For Paul it is a secret now openly shared. “Bow my knees” (v.14) is a physical sign of earnest prayer. Jews usually stood to pray.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 4 begins with “I therefore, a prisoner for the Lord,” turning to how to live.
context.timelineBible: Paul’s language of “breadth and length and height and depth” (v.18) echoes Job 11:7-9, the depth of God’s wisdom. The doxology in v.20-21 is one of Paul’s greatest.
context.sparkNotes: Paul has been entrusted with the mystery that Gentiles are fellow heirs, members of one body, and partakers of the promise in Christ. His task is to preach the unsearchable riches of Christ and show the manifold wisdom of God to the powers. He prays that they be strengthened with power, and know the love of Christ. Glory to him who is able to do far more than we ask or imagine.

translation.meaning: Can’t be tracked, as footprints can’t be traced. The riches of Christ cannot be fully mapped.
Filled to the brim. Paul prays that they be filled with all the fullness of God.

otBackground.note: The measure of God is higher than heaven and deeper than the grave.
All nations will be blessed through Abraham.

overview.summary: Paul explains the mystery that Gentiles are full members of God’s family. He prays for his readers to know the width and depth of Christ’s love.
overview.settingLine: Paul writes as a prisoner for the Gentiles.

history.t: He was held in Rome for two years (Acts 28:30).
Many in Ephesus believed in spirits and magic. Paul says Christ rules over them.

customs.t: Kneeling was an earnest posture for prayer.
“Every family” (v.14) plays on the Greek words for father and family.

archaeology.t: Acts 19 says converts burned magic scrolls. Ephesian letters, amulets, and papyri show magical practice.
Paul lived in a rented house under guard.

overview.discussion: Paul prays that we may know a love that surpasses knowledge. What would it look like to stay rooted in that love in a day full of pressure?
overview.book: The letter to the Ephesians · 6 chapters. A grand view of the church as God’s new family, written from prison.
overview.author: Paul

historicalImage.caption: Paul in Prison, by Rembrandt (1627). It is an imagined scene: Romans was not written from prison, but the painting suits Paul's cry in Romans 7:24.

currentImage.caption: Part of the brick wall of the Castra Praetoria, the barracks of the Praetorian Guard in Rome, built under the emperor Tiberius about AD 23. In Philippians 1:13 Paul says the whole palace guard knew he was in chains for Christ.
